title: In the city: places and directions
goal: Name places, ask for directions, and master one small machine that runs through the rest of the course: **prepositions that merge with articles**.
bekal: ask for and understand simple directions
use *ficar* — the Brazilian verb for "to be located" and ten other meanings

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Perdido na Avenida Paulista
dialogs.intro: Budi is standing on the sidewalk with a dead phone battery. He walks up to a woman at the bus stop.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Com licença, você pode me ajudar?
lines.id: Excuse me, could you help me?
lines.literal: with permission, you you-can me help?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Onde fica o metrô, por favor?

lines.speaker: Mulher:
lines.text: Fica perto. Você vai reto até a esquina.
lines.id: It's close. Go straight to the corner.
lines.literal: it-is-located near. you you-go straight until the corner.

lines.speaker: Mulher:
lines.text: Depois vira à direita, na frente do banco.
lines.id: Then turn right, in front of the bank.
lines.literal: after turn to-the right, in-the front of-the bank.

lines.speaker: Mulher:
lines.text: Não, uns cinco minutos a pé.
lines.id: No, about five minutes on foot.
lines.literal: no, some five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: E tem uma farmácia por aqui?
lines.id: And is there a pharmacy around here?
lines.literal: and it-has a pharmacy by here?

lines.speaker: Mulher:
lines.text: Tem, ao lado da padaria, do outro lado da rua.
lines.id: There is, next to the bakery, across the street.
lines.literal: it-has, to-the side of-the bakery, of-the other side of-the street.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Muito obrigado! Você salvou o meu dia.
lines.id: Thank you so much! You saved my day.
lines.literal: much thanked! you you-saved the my day.

notes: **Ficar is the most Brazilian verb in this whole course.** Its basic meaning is "to stay, to be", but it's used for a dozen things: **to be located** (*Onde fica o metrô?*), **to become** (*Fiquei feliz* = I got happy), **to stay** (*Vou ficar em casa*), and even **to hook up casually** (*ficar com alguém*) — that last one is typical Brazilian youth slang, with no exact equivalent anywhere. To ask where something is, *ficar* is used far more often than *estar*.

**Imagina!** is a typically Brazilian reply to thanks. Literally "imagine!", it means "oh, don't mention it". Along with *de nada* and *por nada*, it's one of three ways to answer *obrigado* — and the warmest.
**Uns cinco minutos** = "about five minutes". Putting *uns/umas* before a number makes it an estimate: *umas dez pessoas* (about ten people). It's the shortest way to avoid sounding too exact.

**À direita, with a grave accent.** The mark on `à` isn't decoration: it shows that the preposition *a* has merged with the article *a*. Two *a*'s become one letter with a backward accent. The rule is set out in the table below.
**Tá** is a shortened *está*, and here it means "okay". You'll hear it at the end of almost every Brazilian sentence: *Vamos, tá?*

grammars.title: Em + article: the first machine
body: *Em* means "in, at, on". It **must** merge with the article that follows — writing them separately is a mistake, not a style choice.
after: **Country and city names follow their own article rules.** *No Brasil*, *no Japão*, *na Indonésia*, *na França* — because those countries take an article. But cities almost never do: *em São Paulo*, *em Jacarta*, *em Lisboa*, with nothing in front.
⚠️ One exception to memorize: **em casa** means "at home" (your own), with no article. *Estou em casa* = I'm at home. If you say *estou na casa*, people will ask "whose house?"

grammars.title: A + article: the second machine
body: *A* means "to" (direction) and "at" (time). It merges the same way, but the result can carry an accent.
after: **The mark on à is called crase, and it doesn't change the sound at all** — *à* and *a* are said exactly the same. It's only a spelling sign that two words have merged. Brazilians themselves often put it in the wrong place, so don't worry too much; what matters is that you can read it.

**In Brazil, para is used more than a for direction.** *Vou para o Rio* sounds more natural than *Vou ao Rio*. And *para* merges too, but only in speech: *pro* (para+o) and *pra* (para+a). You'll see *pra* written everywhere on Brazilian social media, even though grammar books don't accept it yet.

grammars.title: Prepositions of place
body: Everything ending in *de* merges with the next article, so watch for *do* and *da* popping up again and again.
after: Full examples: *O banco fica ao lado **da** padaria* (The bank is next to the bakery), *A chave está em cima **da** mesa* (The key is on the table), *Eu moro perto **do** metrô* (I live near the subway).
⚠️ Notice *entre* — it's the only one in the list that does **not** take *de*: *entre o banco e a farmácia* (between the bank and the pharmacy).

blocks.text: Learn them with their articles, as always.

⚠️ *O banheiro* is the word you'll need most and the easiest to mispronounce. *Onde fica o banheiro?* — memorize it whole right now. In Brazil it's used everywhere, from restaurants to offices; *toalete* sounds like you're reading an airport sign.
⚠️ Notice the transport pattern: **de** ônibus, **de** carro, **de** metrô, **de** avião — but **a** pé for walking. One exception, and it's the one used most.

The sentence *Estou perdido* is much more useful than it looks. In Brazil, saying it to a stranger on the street almost always gets you more help than you need — sometimes they'll walk you right to your destination.

items: I study every day → *Eu estudo todo dia*
Where do you work? → *Onde você trabalha?*
I like coffee → *Eu gosto de café*
We dance every Saturday → *Nós dançamos todo sábado*
Everybody dances in Brazil → *Todo mundo dança no Brasil*

exercises.prompt: Merge the preposition with the article.
Fill in the blanks with the right merged form.
items: O livro está ____ mesa. (em cima de)
A farmácia fica ____ padaria. (ao lado de)
The bank is next to the bakery.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: reto / vai / esquina / até / você / a
banco / fica / do / lado / a / farmácia / ao

answers: no banco — na rua — num restaurante — ao mercado — à esquerda — da padaria
no — na — em cima da — ao lado da — ao — à
